_comment: Stage 1 removal plan (reduction_mode='schur'): fold the core shells of MoS2 into the remaining basis.
The Schur complement keeps the effect of the removed orbitals on the kept ones, so it is the right choice for core states that hybridise weakly but are not negligible.
* 'rules' is a list; the orbitals selected by all rules are removed together.
* Each rule picks atoms with 'target_elements' (chemical symbols) and/or 'target_atom_indices' (0-based, intersected with the elements). If both are missing the rule applies to every atom.

* 'remove_shells' removes single shells. 'Ns' means the N-th shell with that l IN THE BASIS, counted per l in the order of 'elements_orbital_map' in the input info.json: it is NOT the principal quantum number.
* 'remove_orbitals' removes every shell of an l family ('s', 'p', 'd', 'f', 'g', 'h').
* Keys starting with '_' (like this one) are ignored by the parser and are only documentation.

The selectors below assume an FHI-aims basis, where the minimal (atomic) basis comes first for each l and the hydrogenic tier functions after it. Check 'elements_orbital_map' in info.json before reusing this file with another basis set or code.
To adapt it to other elements, list the core shells of each element and count them per l, e.g. Si core (1s 2s 2p) -> ['1s', '2s', '1p'].

rules._comment: Mo core [Kr] 1s-4s, 2p-4p, 3d. Counted per l: s 1..4 = 1s 2s 3s 4s, p 1..3 = 2p 3p 4p, d 1 = 3d. Valence 5s and 4d plus all tier functions are kept.
S core [Ne] 1s 2s 2p. Counted per l: s 1..2 = 1s 2s, p 1 = 2p. Valence 3s and 3p plus all tier functions are kept.
